endpoints.summary: Show the identity behind the current credential
endpoints.description: Returns the identity of the authenticated user: user id, email, name, role, buyer_id and staff flag. Useful to confirm which user and buyer the CLI is acting as.
endpoints.response: 200 with {id, email, name, role, buyer_id, is_staff}.

endpoints.summary: Show the RISK_SCORE condition of an approval step
endpoints.description: Shows the rating_labels that trigger a RISK_SCORE approval step. Get the setting_approval_step_id from `settings approval-step list|show`. Requires the manager role or above.
endpoints.response: 200 with {id, rating_labels}. rating_labels is the array of risk score labels (e.g. ["A","B"]) that trigger the step. 404 Rails default {status, error} when setting_approval_step_id is unknown OR belongs to another buyer (the lookup is scoped to the caller's buyer); 403 {error} when the policy denies access by role; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: Replace the rating_labels of a RISK_SCORE approval step
endpoints.description: Replaces the rating_labels that trigger one RISK_SCORE approval step. Get the setting_approval_step_id from `settings approval-step list|show`. IMPORTANT — this call ALWAYS clears every setting_category linked to the step (via `settings approval-step condition setting-category update`) as a side effect, even when you only touch rating_labels and the step's condition has nothing to do with setting_category: this mirrors a pre-existing quirk of the backend and is deliberately left as-is, not treated as a bug to fix here. If the step also had setting_category links, re-link them afterwards. The whole call (clearing the category links and validating rating_labels) is wrapped in one transaction, so a rejected update (422) leaves both rating_labels and the category links untouched. Requires the manager role or above, same as show.

params.name: rating_labels
params.desc: Full list of risk score labels that trigger the step (e.g. ["A","B"]). Required and non-empty for a RISK_SCORE step — sending an empty array is rejected with 422, it does not clear the labels.

endpoints.response: 200 with the updated {id, rating_labels} (same shape as `settings approval-step condition risk-score show`). 422 {errors} when rating_labels is empty; 400 Rails default {status, error} when the setting_approval_step root is missing entirely; 404 Rails default {status, error} when setting_approval_step_id is unknown OR belongs to another buyer (scoped lookup); 403 {error} when the policy denies access by role; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: Show the SETTING_CATEGORY condition of an approval step
endpoints.description: Shows the setting_categories that trigger a SETTING_CATEGORY approval step. Get the setting_approval_step_id from `settings approval-step list|show`. Requires the manager role or above.
endpoints.response: 200 with {id, setting_category_ids}, ordered by id. setting_category_ids come from `settings category list`. 404 Rails default {status, error} when setting_approval_step_id is unknown OR belongs to another buyer (the lookup is scoped to the caller's buyer); 403 {error} when the policy denies access by role; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: Replace the setting_categories linked to a SETTING_CATEGORY approval step
endpoints.description: Replaces the FULL list of setting_categories that trigger one SETTING_CATEGORY approval step — this is a total replacement, never a merge: the backend deletes every existing link before applying the ones you send. To add one category to a step that already has two linked, you must resend all three setting_category_ids. Each setting_category_id comes from `settings category list` and must belong to the caller's buyer, or the request 404s before anything is deleted. IMPORTANT — sending setting_approval_steps_setting_categories_attributes as an empty array [] is the explicit, intentional way to clear every link, and it succeeds; but omitting the setting_approval_step root from the request body ENTIRELY also clears every link (returns 200 with an empty setting_category_ids) — there is no partial add/remove and no safe empty body, only an explicit clear or the full desired list. Sending the root as an empty object ({}) behaves the same as omitting it: every link is cleared with a 200. The clearing and the update are wrapped in one transaction, so a rejected update (422) leaves the existing links untouched. Requires the manager role or above, same as show.

params.name: setting_approval_steps_setting_categories_attributes
params.desc: JSON array of category objects [{"setting_category_id":"<uuid>"}] — the FULL desired list, not a delta. Pass [] to clear every link. setting_category_id comes from `settings category list` and must belong to the caller's buyer, or the whole request 404s.

endpoints.response: 200 with the updated {id, setting_category_ids} — including when the setting_approval_step root is absent or an empty object, which clears every link and still answers 200 (same shape as `settings approval-step condition setting-category show`). 422 {errors} when a setting_category_id entry is present but null (fails the join's required association); 404 Rails default {status, error} when setting_approval_step_id is unknown, belongs to another buyer, OR any setting_category_id belongs to another buyer (both lookups are buyer-scoped); 403 {error} when the policy denies access by role; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: Show the SETTING_DOCUMENT condition of an approval step
endpoints.description: Shows the setting_documents that trigger a SETTING_DOCUMENT approval step. Get the setting_approval_step_id from `settings approval-step list|show`. Requires the manager role or above.
endpoints.response: 200 with {id, setting_document_ids}, ordered by id. setting_document_ids are Settings::SettingDocument ids — sourced from `settings check list` / `settings certificate list` (forms have no listing command yet). 404 Rails default {status, error} when setting_approval_step_id is unknown OR belongs to another buyer (the lookup is scoped to the caller's buyer); 403 {error} when the policy denies access by role; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: Replace the setting_documents linked to a SETTING_DOCUMENT approval step
endpoints.description: Replaces the FULL list of setting_documents that trigger one SETTING_DOCUMENT approval step — this is a total replacement, never a merge: the backend deletes every existing link before applying the ones you send. To add one document to a step that already has two linked, you must resend all three setting_document_ids. Each setting_document_id is a Settings::SettingDocument id (see `settings check list` / `settings certificate list`) and must belong to the caller's buyer, or the request 404s before anything is deleted. IMPORTANT — sending setting_approval_steps_setting_documents_attributes as an empty array [] is the explicit, intentional way to clear every link, and it succeeds; but omitting the setting_approval_step root from the request body ENTIRELY also clears every link (returns 200 with an empty setting_document_ids) — there is no partial add/remove and no safe empty body, only an explicit clear or the full desired list. Sending the root as an empty object ({}) behaves the same as omitting it: every link is cleared with a 200. The clearing and the update are wrapped in one transaction, so a rejected update (422) leaves the existing links untouched. Requires the manager role or above, same as show.

params.name: setting_approval_steps_setting_documents_attributes
params.desc: JSON array of document objects [{"setting_document_id":"<uuid>"}] — the FULL desired list, not a delta. Pass [] to clear every link. setting_document_id is a Settings::SettingDocument id (see `settings check list` / `settings certificate list`) and must belong to the caller's buyer, or the whole request 404s.

endpoints.response: 200 with the updated {id, setting_document_ids} — including when the setting_approval_step root is absent or an empty object, which clears every link and still answers 200 (same shape as `settings approval-step condition setting-document show`). 422 {errors} when a setting_document_id entry is present but null (fails the join's required association); 404 Rails default {status, error} when setting_approval_step_id is unknown, belongs to another buyer, OR any setting_document_id belongs to another buyer (both lookups are buyer-scoped); 403 {error} when the policy denies access by role; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: Create an approval step
endpoints.description: Creates an approval step for the buyer. IMPORTANT: when `action` is TIERS_APPROVAL the backend automatically seeds one default tier ("Nível Único Padrão") — you do not pass tiers here, and a tiers step without a tier would be invalid. A step is created NOT in use; putting it to work is done elsewhere. Both the uppercase value (RISK_SCORE) and the lowercase key (risk_score) are accepted on input, and the response always reads back the lowercase form. Requires the manager role or above.

params.name: display_name
params.desc: Name of the approval step.

params.name: condition
params.desc: What triggers the step. One of SETTING_CATEGORY, RISK_SCORE, SETTING_DOCUMENT, EXCEPTION_APPROVAL (the lowercase key is also accepted).

params.name: action
params.desc: What the step does. One of AUTOMATIC_APPROVAL, AUTOMATIC_REFUSAL, TIERS_APPROVAL (the lowercase key is also accepted). With condition EXCEPTION_APPROVAL only TIERS_APPROVAL is valid.

params.name: being_used
params.desc: Whether the step is already in use. Defaults to false (a draft).

endpoints.response: 200 with the created {id, display_name, condition, action, being_used}. 422 {errors} on validation (missing display_name/condition/action, or an action other than TIERS_APPROVAL when the condition is EXCEPTION_APPROVAL); 400 Rails default {status, error} when the setting_approval_step root is missing; 403 {error} when the policy denies access; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: Create a rejection reason
endpoints.description: Creates a rejection reason for the buyer. The name must be unique within the buyer. Requires the admin role or above (listing is manager+).

params.name: display_name
params.desc: Name of the rejection reason (e.g. "Risco financeiro"). Must be unique among the buyer's reasons.

endpoints.response: 200 with the created {id, display_name}. 422 {errors} when the name is blank or already used by this buyer; 400 Rails default {status, error} when the setting_approval_steps_decision_reason root is missing; 403 {error} when the policy denies access; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: Delete a rejection reason
endpoints.description: Deletes one rejection reason by its id (see `settings approval-step decision-reason list`). IMPORTANT: the backend refuses to delete the buyer's LAST remaining reason — an approval step rejection would have nothing to pick — and answers 403 in that case, not 422. Check the list length before deleting. Requires the admin role or above.
endpoints.response: 200 echoing the deleted {id, display_name}. 403 {error} when it is the buyer's last remaining reason, when the reason belongs to another buyer, or when the policy denies access; 404 if the id is unknown; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: List the rejection reasons available to approval steps
endpoints.description: Lists the buyer's rejection reasons (motivos de reprovação), ordered by display_name. These are the reasons an approver picks when refusing a supplier in an approval step. Returns the whole collection — this list is not paginated. There is no `show`: the list already carries every field. Requires the manager role or above.
endpoints.response: 200 with an array of {id, display_name}. 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires manager or above).

endpoints.summary: Rename a rejection reason
endpoints.description: Renames one rejection reason by its id — get the id from `settings approval-step decision-reason list`. Requires the admin role or above.

params.name: display_name
params.desc: New name of the rejection reason. Must be unique among the buyer's reasons.

endpoints.response: 200 with the updated {id, display_name}. 422 {errors} when the name is blank or already used; 400 Rails default {status, error} when the root is missing; 404 if the id is unknown; 403 {error} when the reason belongs to another buyer or the policy denies access; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: List the buyer's approval steps
endpoints.description: Lists the buyer's approval steps (etapas de aprovação), newest first. By default returns the steps NOT in use (drafts); pass --current_tab with any value to list the ones in use instead. Optional --search filters by display_name (partial match). Returns the whole collection — this list is not paginated. Requires the manager role or above.

params.name: current_tab
params.desc: Omit to list the steps not in use (being_used false); pass any value (e.g. 'being_used') to list the ones in use.

endpoints.response: 200 with an array of {id, display_name, condition, action, being_used}. `condition` and `action` come back as lowercase keys (e.g. risk_score, automatic_approval) even when created with the uppercase form. 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires manager or above).

endpoints.summary: Show one approval step
endpoints.description: Shows one approval step by its id — get the id from `settings approval-step list`. Requires the manager role or above.
endpoints.response: 200 with {id, display_name, condition, action, being_used, rating_labels, setting_category_ids, setting_document_ids, tiers}. `rating_labels` is the risk score labels that trigger the step (only meaningful when condition is RISK_SCORE; otherwise it still comes back with its default [A, B, C, D, E]). `setting_category_ids` / `setting_document_ids` are the ids linked to the step's condition (only meaningful when condition is SETTING_CATEGORY / SETTING_DOCUMENT respectively; empty array otherwise, never omitted). `tiers` is an array of {id, display_name, user_ids} — only populated when action is TIERS_APPROVAL; a tier just seeded by `settings approval-step create` comes back with an empty user_ids and needs `settings approval-step tier update` to gain approvers. 404 Rails default {status, error} when the id is unknown OR belongs to another buyer (the lookup is scoped to the caller's buyer, so a foreign id never resolves); 403 {error} when the policy denies access by role; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: Add a level (tier) to a TIERS_APPROVAL step
endpoints.description: Creates a new tier under one approval step. Get the setting_approval_step_id from `settings approval-step list|show`. Approvers, if any, are set via setting_approval_steps_tiers_users_attributes, whose user_id comes from `settings company-user list`. Requires the admin role or above (listing is manager+).

params.name: display_name
params.desc: Name of the tier (e.g. "Nível 2").

params.name: setting_approval_steps_tiers_users_attributes
params.desc: JSON array of approver objects [{"user_id":"<uuid>"}]; user_id comes from `settings company-user list` and must belong to the caller's buyer. Omit for a tier with no approvers yet.

endpoints.response: 200 with the created {id, display_name, user_ids}. 422 {errors} when display_name is blank; 400 Rails default {status, error} when the setting_approval_steps_tier root is missing; 404 Rails default {status, error} when setting_approval_step_id is unknown, belongs to another buyer, OR any user_id in setting_approval_steps_tiers_users_attributes does not belong to the caller's buyer (both lookups are buyer-scoped, so a foreign id never resolves); 403 {error} when the policy denies access by role; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: Delete a level (tier) from a TIERS_APPROVAL step
endpoints.description: Deletes one tier by its id (see `settings approval-step tier list`). IMPORTANT: the backend refuses to delete a step's LAST remaining tier — a TIERS_APPROVAL step would have nothing to route through — and answers 403 in that case, not 422. Check the list length before deleting. Requires the admin role or above.
endpoints.response: 200 echoing the deleted {id, display_name, user_ids}. 403 {error} when it is the step's last remaining tier, or when the policy denies access by role; 404 Rails default {status, error} when the tier id is unknown or belongs to another buyer (scoped lookup); 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: List the levels (tiers) of a TIERS_APPROVAL step
endpoints.description: Lists the approval levels (tiers) of one approval step, ordered by creation. Get the setting_approval_step_id from `settings approval-step list|show`. Requires the manager role or above.
endpoints.response: 200 with an array of {id, display_name, user_ids}. A freshly seeded tier (from `settings approval-step create` with action TIERS_APPROVAL) comes back with an empty user_ids and needs `settings approval-step tier update` to gain approvers. 404 Rails default {status, error} when setting_approval_step_id is unknown OR belongs to another buyer (the lookup is scoped to the caller's buyer); 403 {error} when the policy denies access by role; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: Rename a tier or replace its approvers
endpoints.description: Updates one tier by its id (see `settings approval-step tier list`). IMPORTANT — setting_approval_steps_tiers_users_attributes is a TOTAL REPLACEMENT of the tier's approvers, never a merge: the backend deletes every existing approver before applying the ones you send, so re-sending only a subset drops the rest, and calling update WITHOUT this param at all still deletes every approver and returns success — there is no partial add/remove. To add one approver to a tier that already has two, you must resend all three user_ids; to keep the current approvers unchanged, resend the same list back. This param is declared required here specifically to force that choice on every call — passing an empty array is the explicit way to clear all approvers. Each user_id must belong to the caller's buyer (see `settings company-user list`), or the request 404s before anything is deleted. Requires the admin role or above.

params.name: display_name
params.desc: New name of the tier.

params.name: setting_approval_steps_tiers_users_attributes
params.desc: JSON array of approver objects [{"user_id":"<uuid>"}] — the FULL desired list of approvers, not a delta. Pass [] to remove every approver. user_id comes from `settings company-user list` and must belong to the caller's buyer.

endpoints.response: 200 with the updated {id, display_name, user_ids}. 422 {errors} when display_name is blank — the whole update is wrapped in a transaction, so a rejected update leaves the existing approvers untouched; 400 Rails default {status, error} when the setting_approval_steps_tier root is missing; 404 Rails default {status, error} when the tier id is unknown, belongs to another buyer, OR any user_id in setting_approval_steps_tiers_users_attributes does not belong to the caller's buyer; 403 {error} when the policy denies access by role; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: Update an approval step
endpoints.description: Updates one approval step by its id (see `settings approval-step list`). Only the fields you pass change. Same enum rules as `create`. Requires the manager role or above.

params.name: display_name
params.desc: New name of the approval step.

params.name: condition
params.desc: What triggers the step. One of SETTING_CATEGORY, RISK_SCORE, SETTING_DOCUMENT, EXCEPTION_APPROVAL (the lowercase key is also accepted).

params.name: action
params.desc: What the step does. One of AUTOMATIC_APPROVAL, AUTOMATIC_REFUSAL, TIERS_APPROVAL (the lowercase key is also accepted).

params.name: being_used
params.desc: Whether the step is in use.

endpoints.response: 200 with the updated {id, display_name, condition, action, being_used}. 422 {errors} on validation (e.g. a blank display_name); 400 Rails default {status, error} when the setting_approval_step root is missing; 404 Rails default {status, error} when the id is unknown OR belongs to another buyer (scoped lookup); 403 {error} when the policy denies access by role; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: Export the suppliers' bank information answers to CSV
endpoints.description: Starts the CSV export of every supplier's bank information answer to this document. The export runs in background and REPLACES the previously attached file (has_one_attached), so the old `report_csv_url` stops working the moment this is called. The CSV carries sensitive data — each supplier's account CPF/CNPJ, branch, account number and a one-week signed link to the bank statement — so it is admin-only: the finished file is not in this response, poll `settings bank-information show <id>` until `report_csv_url` appears (returned only to an admin) and download from there. bank_information_id comes from `settings bank-information list`; only the enabled document exports (a disabled one answers 404). Requires the admin role or above.
endpoints.response: 200 with {id, name, display_name, export_enqueued: true}. The file URL shows up later in `settings bank-information show` as `report_csv_url`, only for an admin. 404 Rails default {status, error} when bank_information_id is unknown, disabled, or belongs to another buyer; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires the admin role or above); 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: List the buyer's bank information documents
endpoints.description: Lists the buyer's bank information documents (dados bancários — SettingBankInformation), ordered by display order then display_name. A buyer has at most one enabled bank information document. By default returns the enabled documents; pass --tab disabled to list the archived (disabled) ones instead. Each item carries the applicability flags national_pj/national_pf/international, which tell for which category legal_entity (PJ / PF / INTERNATIONAL) the document is available. This is a source of the `setting_document_id` a future `settings category risk create` will need: pick a document whose applicability flag matches the category's legal_entity (national_pj for a PJ category, national_pf for PF, international for INTERNATIONAL).

params.name: tab
params.desc: Which set to list: omit (or any value other than 'disabled') for enabled documents, or 'disabled' for archived ones.

endpoints.response: 200 with an array of {id, display_name, disabled, national_pj, national_pf, international, setting_grouper_id, type, type_humanize, order}. The three boolean flags mark the category legal_entities (PJ / PF / INTERNATIONAL) the document applies to. 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires manager or above).

endpoints.summary: Show the bank information document with its editable settings
endpoints.description: Shows one bank information document (dados bancários) of the buyer by its id — get the id from `settings bank-information list`. On top of the list fields it returns everything `settings bank-information update` can change, plus the nested `setting_document_review` (`review_type` and `expires_on_in_days`). Requires the manager role or above.
endpoints.response: 200 with {id, display_name, disabled, national_pj, national_pf, international, setting_grouper_id, type, type_humanize, order, renew_at_in_days, allow_pf_bank_account, block_supplier_on_expiry, send_document_reviewed_event, webhook_reference, setting_document_review:{id, review_type, expires_on_in_days}}. `report_csv_url` is returned only to an admin who has run `settings bank-information export-report` and only while the export is attached — the CSV carries each supplier's account CPF/CNPJ, branch, account number and a one-week signed link to the bank statement, so it stays behind the admin-only export gate rather than the manager-level read. 404 Rails default {status, error} when the id is unknown OR belongs to another buyer (scoped lookup); 403 {error} when the policy denies access by role; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: Update the bank information document
endpoints.description: Updates one bank information document by its id (see `settings bank-information list`). Only the fields you pass change. There is no create/destroy for this document — the buyer has it from the start, you only configure it. Requires the admin role or above (reading is manager+).

params.name: display_name
params.desc: Label shown to the supplier.

params.name: renew_at_in_days
params.desc: Days after approval when the document must be renewed (0 = never).

params.name: allow_pf_bank_account
params.desc: Whether a supplier may inform a personal (PF) bank account.

params.name: setting_grouper_id
params.desc: Id of the review group that reviews this document — from `settings setting-grouper list`. Must belong to the same buyer.

params.name: block_supplier_on_expiry
params.desc: Whether the supplier is blocked when this document expires.

params.name: send_document_reviewed_event
params.desc: Whether a webhook event is emitted when this document is reviewed.

params.name: webhook_reference
params.desc: Free-text reference sent along with the webhook event.

params.name: setting_document_review_attributes
params.desc: JSON object with the nested review settings. Requires the review's own `id` (from `settings bank-information show`) plus the field to change, e.g. '{"id":"<review-id>","expires_on_in_days":90}'. `expires_on_in_days` must be one of 0, 30, 90, 180, 360, 720, 1080.

endpoints.response: 200 with the updated document in the same shape as `settings bank-information show`. 422 {errors} on validation (e.g. an expires_on_in_days outside the allowed set); 400 Rails default {status, error} when the setting_bank_information root is missing; 404 Rails default {status, error} when the id is unknown OR belongs to another buyer (scoped lookup); 403 {error} when the policy denies access by role; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: Create a document field
endpoints.description: Creates a new document field for the buyer. field_type must be one of: currency, select, text_input, upload, multi_select. When field_type is select or multi_select, options must contain at least 2 entries. level must be one of: supplier, qualification (default supplier). display_name is required; name is auto-generated from display_name when omitted.

params.name: display_name
params.desc: Human-readable label of the field (required, unique per buyer among enabled fields).

params.name: name
params.desc: Internal identifier (unique per buyer). Auto-generated from display_name when omitted.

params.name: hint
params.desc: Optional helper text shown alongside the field.

params.name: field_type
params.desc: Field type. One of: currency, select, text_input, upload, multi_select. select and multi_select require options with at least 2 entries.

params.name: level
params.desc: Scope of the field. One of: supplier, qualification. Defaults to supplier.

params.name: national_pf
params.desc: Available for national individual (PF) suppliers. Defaults to true.

params.name: national_pj
params.desc: Available for national company (PJ) suppliers. Defaults to true.

params.name: international
params.desc: Available for international suppliers. Defaults to true.

params.name: availability_on_request
params.desc: Visibility in supplier requests. One of: hidden, optional, required. Defaults to hidden.

params.name: availability_on_qualification
params.desc: Visibility during qualification. One of: hidden, optional, required. Defaults to hidden.

params.name: options
params.desc: Array of string options. Required (at least 2) when field_type is select or multi_select.

endpoints.response: 200 with {id, name, display_name, field_type, level, disabled, order}. 422 {errors} on validation (e.g. missing display_name, or select/multi_select without at least 2 options); 400 Rails default {status, error} when the setting_buyer_document body root is missing; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires admin or above); 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: Disable (archive) a buyer document field
endpoints.description: Disables an enabled buyer document field for the buyer, archiving the setting. When `disable_buyer_documents` is true, the associated buyer documents are archived as well. The `id` identifies the enabled SettingBuyerDocument to disable — resolve it from `settings buyer-document list` (pending, plan P1). A row lock serializes concurrent or retried disable calls for the same id: only the first one takes effect, and every later one 404s instead of re-running the cascade.

params.name: disable_buyer_documents
params.desc: When true, also archives the buyer documents associated with the field

endpoints.response: 200 with the disabled document {id, name, display_name, field_type, level, disabled, order}. 404 Rails default {status, error} if no enabled document matches the id, including a concurrent/retried disable call for the same id that lost the race; 400 Rails default {status, error} when disable_buyer_documents is missing; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (caller below admin); 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: Enable (unarchive) a buyer document field
endpoints.description: Enables a previously disabled buyer document field for the buyer, unarchiving the setting and its associated buyer documents. The `id` identifies the disabled SettingBuyerDocument to enable — resolve it from `settings buyer-document list` (pending, plan P1; use the disabled/archived listing).

params.name: id
params.desc: The id of the disabled SettingBuyerDocument to enable (from `settings buyer-document list`)

endpoints.response: 200 with the enabled document {id, name, display_name, field_type, level, disabled, order}. 404 Rails default {status, error} if no disabled document matches the id; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (caller below admin); 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: List the buyer's document fields
endpoints.description: Lists the buyer's supplier/qualification document fields (SettingBuyerDocument), ordered by their display order. By default returns the enabled fields; pass --tab disabled to list the archived (disabled) ones instead. This command is the source of the <id> consumed by `settings buyer-document show` and `settings buyer-document update`.

params.name: tab
params.desc: Which set to list: omit (or any value other than 'disabled') for enabled fields, or 'disabled' for archived ones.

endpoints.response: 200 with an array of {id, name, display_name, field_type, level, disabled, order}. 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires manager or above).

endpoints.summary: Reorder the buyer document fields
endpoints.description: Sets the display order of the buyer's enabled document fields. `identifiers` is a comma-separated list of SettingBuyerDocument ids in the desired final order; ids not belonging to the buyer are ignored. Resolve the ids from `settings buyer-document list` (pending, plan P1) and pass them in the order you want.
